problems.problem: The regenerated wall still reads as large-format stone slabs, not monolithic cleft flint: a continuous horizontal joint runs across the wall at roughly y=535 (visible left and right of the cap) with vertical joints near x=270 and x=965, and the support is a raised tabletop whose honed front face fills the bottom band below y≈1290. The brief's 'monolithic cleft flint plane with matte mineral grain and split-plane facets' is instead a smooth slabbed niche, so the mineral concept stays under-delivered versus the seamless material fields in references 3-5.

Direction disagreement persists in softened form: the broad oblique gradient rakes from upper left while the cutout's own studio light is frontal and symmetric (equal vertical highlights on both glass edges, specular collar streaks centered), and the contact detail (crop 28,1099-621,1349) shows the soft ambient contact shadow centered under the foot with no lateral bias or caustic. Contact is genuine and offset_y=0 is correct, but the scene light direction and the product's recorded illumination still do not fully agree.

The right column still does not close as an editorial unit: the rust rule sits at y=800, leaving a ~300px dead wall gap between the rule and the tabletop while the title block ends at y=774; logo (bbox 610,504-736,528) against 74px title lines gives a thin brand head, so hierarchy from brand to name to rule reads spaced apart rather than locked.

changes.value: One seamless monolithic cleft flint stone wall in cool bone grey, matte split-plane facets and fine mineral grain, no joints no seams no slabs no tiles no grout lines, rising from a continuous honed pale stone ground that fills the lower quarter of the frame edge to edge with no visible front edge and no tabletop, even soft frontal diffuse daylight from camera direction, one very gentle broad oblique tonal gradient softening the upper left of the wall, shadowless ambient illumination, empty scene, no objects
